When a Galactic Alliance strike force rescued Page and captured Carr, Page allowed the Yuuzhan Vong commander to survive, but felt that he would likely kill him the next time they met.<ref name="tuf" /> Page saw many deaths throughout his career, and felt that many of his campaigns had happened at the expense of too many lives.<ref name="engage" /> He was not only confident in and trustful of the commandos on his team,<ref name="rogue" /><ref name="darkstryder" /> but was fond of some of them as well.<ref name="endgame" /> He made many other friends in the military,<ref name="httesb" /><ref name="tfp" /><ref name="tuf" /> and when Wedge Antilles believed him dead after Operation: Trinity, the general took it as a hard blow.<ref name="tfp" />

Despite his stature as one of the New Republic's best soldiers, Page was modest<ref name="httesb" /> and respectful to superior officers.<ref name="rogue" /><ref name="gamble" /> He turned down many offers of promotion from his rank of lieutenant<ref name="httesb" /><ref name="gaw" /> as a sign of humility<ref name="cswe" /> and to avoid playing the game of politics. His reluctance was also inspired by Luke Skywalker and Han Solo, both of whom he believed had no use for ranks; Page was a great admirer of Skywalker, Solo, and Leia Organa Solo,<ref name="httesb" /> known colloquially as the [[Heroes of Yavin/Legends|Heroes of Yavin]].<ref name="tabsb" /> In 9 ABY, Page finally accepted a promotion to captain,<ref name="ir" /> but did so grudgingly.<ref name="gaw" /> While in the clutches of the Yuuzhan Vong, Page helped abolish all previous notions of rank among the prisoners of war and wore his filthy prison uniform proudly. He insisted that the other prisoners eat meals before him, but the respect that they had for he and Pash Cracken prompted them to serve the two first.<ref name="tuf" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Can you tell how you got cast as Lieutenant Page for ''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi''?''"<br />"''Just lucky, right time, right place.|Star Wars Interviews talks to David Church|<ref name="church1">{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsinterviews1|url=2010/06/david-church-interview-lieutenant-page.html|name=Star Wars Interviews|text=David Church interview &#124; Lieutenant Page &#124; Star Wars}}</ref>}}
Lieutenant Page was created by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Timothy Zahn]] and appeared briefly in Zahn's [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]''.<ref name="htte" /> [[1992]]'s ''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]'' expanded on the character and his commando team, giving biographical details and establishing him as having fought in the Battle of Hoth,<ref name="httesb" /> an event depicted in the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']].<ref name="esb" /> [[1993]]'s ''[[The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook]]'' placed Page at the Battle of Endor<ref name="mts" /> from the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="rotj" /> The character went on to play minor roles in several other novels published throughout the 1990s,<ref name="rogue" /><ref name="gamble" /><ref name="champs" /> and took on a starring role in the short story ''[[The Saga Begins]]'', published in the [[1995]] [[roleplaying game]] scenario ''[[The DarkStryder Campaign]]''.<ref name="thesagabegins" /> After being briefly mentioned in ''[[The New Jedi Order: The Final Prophecy]]'', the eighteenth and penultimate novel in [[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|''The New Jedi Order'']] book series, Page played a major role in the series' conclusion, ''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''. Both novels were published in [[2003]], and they were the first sources to christen the character "Judder," giving him a first name twelve years after his creation.<ref name="tfp" /><ref name="tuf" />

[[File:AlienPage.jpg|thumb|right|125px|Page's non-Human appearance in the comic adaptation of ''Heir to the Empire'']]
In [[1999]], the [[Endor Limited]] expansion set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]] included a card of Lieutenant Page that [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the character into being an extra glimpsed briefly aboard ''Home One'' in ''Return of the Jedi''.<ref name="ccg" /> The extra was played by [[David Church]], who also portrayed a stormtrooper in [[1977]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']].<ref name="church1" /><ref name="church2">{{YouTube|channel=@ConGuests|name=ConGuests|video=MbTAeFv9-RU|text=Dave Church Stormtrooper Lt Page Star Wars & Return of the Jedi|date=2010-04-03}}</ref> Church discovered that his ''Return of the Jedi'' character had been given a name during a signing at a Collectormania convention.<ref name="church1" />

Although Page's species was established as Human in the ''Heir to the Empire Sourcebook'',<ref name="httesb" /> he appears as a decidedly non-Human character in ''Heir to the Empire''{{'s}} [[Star Wars: Heir to the Empire (comic series)|comic adaptation]]. The series' [[Heir to the Empire 1|first issue]], published in 1995, depicts Page as a ridge-headed alien.<ref name="htte1">[[Heir to the Empire 1|''Heir to the Empire'' 1]]</ref> In the [[1998]] novel ''[[X-Wing: Wraith Squadron]]'', Wedge Antilles suggests that Page's Commandos would be an asset to the New Republic's efforts in the [[Battle of Ession]]. No further mention of Page or his team is made in the novel, although the presence of New Republic commandos on [[Ession]]'s surface is confirmed. It is unclear whether or not Page participated in the battle.<ref name="wraith" />

Page was originally going to be mentioned in the article ''[[Dirty Dozen: The Imperial Grand Admirals]]'', which was set to be published in ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' before that magazine's cancelation.<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|danwallace|16|Grand Admirals: What Have They Got in their Pocketsses?}}</ref> The article established that Page and Admiral Ackbar [[Liberation of Kashyyyk/Legends|liberated]] Kashyyyk from Grand Admiral [[Peccati Syn]] in the early days of the New Republic, and that Page and Wedge Antilles embarked on an information-gathering mission to Boudolayz in a campaign against Grand Admiral [[Afsheen Makati]].<ref name="DD:TIGA">"[[Dirty Dozen: The Imperial Grand Admirals]]"</ref> The article was eventually published in the [[Star Wars Insider 66|sixty-sixth issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' as ''[[Who's Who: Imperial Grand Admirals]]'', but with less information than its original draft and none about Page.<ref name="Blog" /><ref name="grand admiral">{{InsiderCite|66|Who's Who: Imperial Grand Admirals}}</ref> Part 1 of ''[[The Dark Forces Saga]]'', an article published online in [[2005]], [[canon]]ized Page's campaigns at Kashyyyk and Boudolayz, but did not place Ackbar, Antilles, or any Grand Admirals at them.<ref name="dark forces">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050407a|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 1}}</ref>

Page appeared in the roleplaying game supplement ''[[The New Republic Campaign: The Battle for Endor from the PCs' Perspective]]'', published in [[Polyhedron 90|the ninetieth issue]] of ''[[Polyhedron]]'' magazine in 1993. As the magazine was unaffiliated with [[LucasBooks]] at the time,<ref name="areyoukiddingme">{{PolyhedronCite|90|The New Republic Campaign: The Battle for Endor from the PCs' Perspective}}</ref> the scenario and Page's role in it are non-canon.<ref name="Unlicensed">{{UnlicensedStatus}}</ref>
